subject.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove

question: After the package lifecycle is made cross-process safe, should OpenClaw adopt this destructive core Claws status/remove contract, including its session cleanup, persistent ownership ledger, and retained removal history?
rationale: The implementation establishes durable and destructive core behavior across multiple owners while the RFC and prerequisite stack remain open, so code correctness alone cannot choose the permanent recovery and audit contract.

options.title: Sponsor the complete lifecycle
options.body: Approve the direction after shared install/uninstall serialization, retained tombstone semantics, stack-level upgrade review, and focused recovery proof are complete.

options.title: Land status only
options.body: Keep authoritative read-only inventory while deferring destructive removal and its persistence contract to a separately approved slice.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Leave the series unmerged until maintainers select a different ownership, cleanup, or recovery boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the complete lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve the direction after shared install/uninstall serialization, retained tombstone semantics, stack-level upgrade review, and focused recovery proof are complete.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to this PR and already routed the RFC's package-removal ownership requirement into the implementation discussion.
